title: Remapped Keyboard Shortcut Causing a Problem to Other Keys: Existing Issue
author: MMBian
summary: After app-specific Alt+C/Alt+V remaps in Explorer, the physical Delete key can stop working until Keyboard Manager is disabled.

confidence.rationale: Keyboard Manager is implicated, but no trace identifies the stale state.

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied requested evidence; the next discriminator is maintainer-side event tracing.
evidence: The reporter supplied a bug report and video.
A collaborator matched the remap but could not reproduce locally.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete existing fix covers the reported path; the lightweight hypothesis is ready for a bounded design workflow.

actions.label: Trace Delete after remapped copy and paste

steps: Map Alt+C and Alt+V to Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V.
Copy, navigate, paste, then press Delete in Explorer.
reproduce.expected_result: Delete remains functional and no modifier is logically pressed.

proposed_fixes.title: Release synthetic modifier state after remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: An app-specific Alt-to-Ctrl remap may leave a modifier or suppression state active and swallow Delete.
plan: Trace physical and synthetic modifier transitions around copy, paste, navigation, and Delete.
Clear injected modifiers and suppression state on completion and focus transition.
Add a sequence test ending with an unrelated physical key.
verification: Repeat the Explorer sequence and confirm Delete always works.

confidence.rationale: Keyboard Manager is implicated, but no trace identifies the stale state.
